hold_text: FILENAME NOTE: the dispatch named this file `.github/pr-landing/r3-resolver-cost-fidelity.json`. scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py::branch_slug derives the path MECHANICALLY from the branch (`lane/r3-resolver-cost-fidelity` -> `lane-r3-resolver-cost-fidelity`), and claude-pr-automerge.yml uses the same derivation so the two agree; at the dispatched name the guard reports `state=undeclared` and CI fails. The file is therefore at the slug the guard reads, with the dispatched content unchanged. Nothing was widened. Tier-3 because the diff edits config/mandates.yaml, the authorization store for the fully-automated ladder. The operator already DECIDED this change on 2026-09-25 ("Yes, via held PR") and the manager session (session_01Ljhs6sFAdWHdMDhJpL5aBP) merges it; this lane opened the PR, drove CI green and STOPS. It does not merge, does not arm auto-merge (no .github/pr-automerge-requests entry), does not deploy, and takes no merge slot. WHAT THE MERGER IS APPROVING: (1) Tier-2 -- scripts/ops/mandate_resolver.py's two cost clauses read the R3 PER-LEG verdict (RULE-R3-GATE1-COST-FIDELITY-v1) instead of D3's venue point estimate, so `insufficient_n` and `inconclusive` can no longer pass a promotion and only `divergent` fires the demotion; (2) Tier-3 -- the matching `fires_when` wording on MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 and MD-DEMOTE-S1-OFF. Exactly three YAML fields differ from origin/main, verified by parsing both sides: MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2.fires_when, MD-DEMOTE-S1-OFF.fires_when and MD-DEMOTE-S1-OFF.evidence_required. No bar value, no cap, no `blocked_until`, no `never:`, no `direction:`, no grant and no entry in `proposed:` is touched; no mandate is armed or widened. MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 remains blocked_until-truthy and the resolver still REFUSES it with R-MANDATE-BLOCKED. No roster, no account mode, no risk cap, no sizing and no order path is touched, and nothing calls the resolver on a schedule, so merging alters no runtime behaviour.
why: R3 (checklist row R3, PR #12965) registered RULE-R3-GATE1-COST-FIDELITY-v1 and committed the first per-leg record, but nothing read it -- the resolver's cost clause still graded every leg against one number for a whole venue. This makes both clauses read the per-leg verdict, adds the mandate wording that describes it, and fixes a defect found while replacing the reader: the old `latest_d3` globbed `*.json` over a directory holding three artifacts per run and returned the fills pull log, so both clauses were inert (fail-closed) regardless of the data. scripts/ops/mandate_resolver.py + config/mandates.yaml + tests/test_mandate_resolver.py (56 passed) + one doc reconciliation.
